facts.fact: The Government's National Health Compact gives a baseline of 5 health facilities implementing the Electronic Medical Records system against a 2030 target of 1,800, in a network it puts at about 1,463 public facilities including about 24 hospitals; the count is of facilities of all tiers, and the baseline is undated, so the Compact's own date is used.

The National Health Compact of 6 December 2025 names the EMR in its action plan: a costed strategy for the phased roll-out by 2027 and roll-out to all medical facilities by 2030, beginning in high-volume districts and linking PHUs and referral hospitals.
The National Health Compact names the Ministry of Health's Directorate of Policy, Planning and Information as lead institution for the EMR costed strategy and roll-out.
The Government adopted the National Health Compact in Tokyo on 6 December 2025, committing to scale the EMR to all health facilities by 2030 with integration into DHIS2.
